This was amazing. I want to watch a full fledged documentary of anime themed like this. I want colleges to teach classes like this. I actually watched it twice to take it all in. Liked, faved and then subbed, not exaggerating. I'm profoundly affected.

In film (or anime in this case) cinematography is the aspect that excites me the most. Good or bad if a shot does something different it's interesting. Nothing is quite as eye catching as an unexpected camera angle or unexpected use of colour (besides that blue on orange bullshit that Hollywood has been wanking to for the last few years. A wonderful example is the movie 12 Angry Men (Not anime but I'm sure you can handle it). This might be my favourite movie and this bit from wikipedia explains why:

At the beginning of the film, the cameras are positioned above eye level and mounted with wide-angle lenses to give the appearance of greater depth between subjects, but as the film progresses the focal length of the lenses is gradually increased. By the end of the film, nearly everyone is shown in closeup using telephoto lenses from a lower angle, which decreases or "shortens" depth of field. Lumet, who began his career as a director of photography, stated that his intention in using these techniques with cinematographer Boris Kaufman was to create a nearly palpable claustrophobia.

The director has caused a sympathetic connection between the audience and the cast of the movie with nothing but the camera usage, nothing on screen, no dialog, just angles and FOV. This is the movie that made me love movies. Stuff like this is why most beloved directors are beloved. With so much to work with in cinematography, the best find their own unique style or make reference to other great works e.g. Tarantino has taken a million shots from an older French director (name currently alludes me).
